plain_english: The great lords of mantra, the lords of mantra, the mantras headed by Shiva, and the two akala classes together with the sakala class are all powers of Shiva himself.
sanskrit_cite: mahāmantreśamantreśamantrāḥ śivapurogamāḥ akalau sakalaśceti śivasyaiva vibhūtayaḥ

plain_english: The unfailing essential nature of the whole group of principles is the Self alone, for as the revered Trishiro doctrine states, the Self is their very nature.
sanskrit_cite: tattvagrāmasya sarvasya dharmaḥ syādanapāyavān ātmaiva hi svabhāvātmetyuktaṃ śrītriśiromate

plain_english: By the term 'group of principles' is meant that which stands in the heart, in all bodies, and in its own nature, which is very subtle, and which is the collective totality of the principles.
sanskrit_cite: hṛdisthaṃ sarvadehasthaṃ svabhāvasthaṃ susūkṣmakam sāmūhyaṃ caiva tattvānāṃ grāmaśabdena kīrtitam

plain_english: The Self alone is said to be the essential nature: flooded with the nectar of Shiva, it is knowledge abiding in light, beyond the midst of being, nonbeing, and the like.
sanskrit_cite: ātmaiva dharma ityuktaḥ śivāmṛtapariplutaḥ prakāśāvasthitaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvābhāvādimadhyataḥ

plain_english: Abiding in one's own place should be understood as being the seer, free of covering, purified by the pure insight that reveals the distinct reality.
sanskrit_cite: svasthāne vartanaṃ jñeyaṃ draṣṭṛtvaṃ vigatāvṛti viviktavastukathitaśuddhavijñānanirmalaḥ

plain_english: When the functioning of the group-nature is understood, everything is accomplished; abandoning the lower and entering the higher, one becomes established in delight in the middle region.
sanskrit_cite: grāmadharmavṛttiruktastasya sarvaṃ prasiddhyati ūrdhva tyaktvādho viśetsa rāmastho madhyadeśagaḥ

plain_english: Movement and rest, dream and waking, opening and closing, running and leaping, effort, and the feeling of power are all included.
sanskrit_cite: gatiḥ sthānaṃ svapnajāgradunmeṣaṇanimeṣaṇe dhāvanaṃ plavanaṃ caiva āyāsaḥ śaktivedanam

plain_english: The divisions of intellect, states, designations, and manifold actions are all pervaded here by that delight, which is Shiva, the supreme cause.
sanskrit_cite: buddhibhedāstathā bhāvāḥ saṃjñāḥ karmāṇyanekaśaḥ eṣa rāmo vyāpako@tra śivaḥ paramakāraṇam

plain_english: One whose mind is worn down by impurity can, through the mere restraint of memory, meditate on the supreme object of meditation that is present within the state of going and coming.
sanskrit_cite: kalmaṣakṣīṇamanasā smṛtimātranirodhanāt dhyāyate paramaṃ dhyeyaṃ gamāgamapade sthitam

plain_english: One reaches the supreme Shiva, called Bhairava, even through repetition; but true repetition is of that very nature, having fallen away from the states of being and nonbeing.
sanskrit_cite: paraṃ śivaṃ tu vrajati bhairavākhyaṃ japādapi tatsvarūpaṃ japaḥ prokto bhāvābhāvapadacyutaḥ

plain_english: Even here, distinctions such as far and near are fashioned by his freedom and arise in dependence on the freedom of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: tadatrāpi tadīyena svātantryeṇopakalpitaḥ dūrāsannādiko bhedaścitsvātantryavyapekṣayā

plain_english: Thus, because he is full of freedom and able to accomplish even the most difficult deeds, in what form indeed does the supreme Lord not shine?
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ svātantryapūrṇatvādatidurghaṭakāryayam kena nāma na rūpeṇa bhāsate parameśvaraḥ

plain_english: He shines uncovered, he shines with his own nature veiled, and he shines as both veiled and unveiled in many ways through association with difference.
sanskrit_cite: nirāvaraṇamābhāti bhātyābṛtanijātmakaḥ āvṛtānāvṛto bhāti bahudhā bhedasaṃgamāt

plain_english: Thus the triad of powers in the Lord, which is another name for his freedom, has been made manifest by the teachers under names such as will and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: iti śaktitrayaṃ nāthe svātantryāparanāmakam icchādibhirabhikhyābhirgurubhiḥ prakaṭīkṛtam

plain_english: The Lord is taught through meaningful scriptural words as this great Bhairava, the supreme Lord, Pati, and Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: devo hyanvarthaśāstroktaiḥ śabdaiḥ samupadiśyate mahābhairavadevo@yaṃ patiryaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ

plain_english: He bears the universe by filling and sustaining it, he is resorted to with reflective awareness, he is of the nature of sound, and he brings good to those who fear samsara.
sanskrit_cite: viśvaṃ bibharti pūraṇadhāraṇayogena tena ca śriyate savimarśatayā rava rūpataśca saṃsārabhīruhitakṛcca

plain_english: Even from a trembling touch born of fear of worldly existence, a reflective awareness of the fear of becoming can arise in the heart and become manifest through the descent of power.
sanskrit_cite: saṃsārabhītijanitādravātparāmarśato@pi hṛdi jātaḥ prakaṭībhūtaṃ bhavabhayavimarśanaṃ śaktipātato yena

plain_english: He becomes manifest in those who dry up the time principle that drives the stars, and in those whose minds delight in absorption in the devouring of time.
sanskrit_cite: nakṣatraprerakakālatattvasaṃśoṣakāriṇo ye ca kālagrāsasamādhānarasikamanaḥsu teṣu ca prakaṭaḥ

plain_english: Their roaring is for the fear of contracted bound beings—the roaring of the goddesses of one's own senses and also of the fourfold group of khecarī and others, within and without.
sanskrit_cite: saṃkocipaśujanabhiye yāsāṃ ravaṇaṃ svakaraṇadevīnām antarbahiścaturvidhakhecaryādikagaṇasyāpi

plain_english: The lord of that group, greatly terrifying because he shatters the activity of worldly existence, is praised in the scripture by the teachers as Bhairava through these etymological meanings.
sanskrit_cite: tasya svāmī saṃsāravṛttivighaṭanamahābhīmaḥ bhairava iti gurubhirimairanvarthaiḥ saṃstutaḥ śāstre

plain_english: Where there is no talk of what is to be rejected or accepted, there is play as the overflowing mass of one's own bliss, the will to abide in supremacy over all, and likewise autonomy.
sanskrit_cite: heyopādeyakathāvirahe svānandaghanatayocchalanam krīḍā sarvotkarṣeṇavartanecchā tathā svatantratvam

plain_english: Even in the undivided self, activity appears through difference as articulate expression; and because all manifestation illumines him, everything becomes his praise.
sanskrit_cite: vyavaharaṇamabhinne@pi svātmani bhedena saṃjalpaḥ nikhilāvabhāsanācca dyotanamasya stutiryataḥ sakalam

plain_english: From the attainment of selfhood onward, in everything that is to be done, the course becomes inclined toward him—consisting of awareness, made of all action, and endowed with the powers of knowing and doing.
sanskrit_cite: tatpravaṇamātmalābhātprabhṛti samaste@pi kartavye bodhātmakaḥ samastakriyāmayo dṛkkriyāguṇaśca gatiḥ

plain_english: Thus, by etymological explanations in the scripture whose body is Śiva, the teachers remember the deity; because he teaches, restrains, protects, and matures, he benefits all. Therefore he is the Lord, Śiva himself consisting of the highest good, and there is nothing there that is not Śiva.
sanskrit_cite: iti nirvacanaiḥ śivatanuśāstre gurubhiḥ smṛto devaḥ śāsanarodhanapālanapācanayogātsa sarvamupakurute tena patiḥ śreyomaya eva śivo nāśivaṃ kimapi tatra

plain_english: Since such a form may shine even to some extent in Rudra, Upendra, and others, the qualifier 'supreme and great state' is assumed for the one who removes limitation.
sanskrit_cite: īdṛgrūpaṃ kiyadapi rudropendrādiṣu sphuredyena tenāvacchedanude paramamahatpadaviśeṣaṇamupāttam

plain_english: Thus, that true principle to be known is shown by me, by the command of Śiva, through one's own awareness, sound reasoning, the Lord's scripture, and the sequence of the Trika.
sanskrit_cite: iti yajjñeyasatattvaṃ darśyate tacchivājñayā mayā svasaṃvitsattarkapatiśāstratrikakramāt

plain_english: His three powers, beginning with parā, shine in emission, maintenance, resorption, and the fourth; therefore these are declared as twelve.
sanskrit_cite: tasya śaktaya evaitāstisro bhānti parādikāḥ sṛṣṭau sthitau laye turye tenaitā dvādaśoditāḥ

plain_english: This one, of such full nature, is called the supreme Śiva; therefore worshippers are directly and fully established right there.
sanskrit_cite: tāvānpūrṇasvabhāvo@sau paramaḥ śiva ucyate tenātropāsakāḥ sākṣāttatraiva pariniṣṭhitāḥ

plain_english: Even the arrangement of their divisions, parts, deficiencies, excesses, and so on is set forth in the scriptures solely by the force of his autonomy.
sanskrit_cite: tāsāmapi ca bhedāṃśanyūnādhikyādiyojanam tatsvātantryabalādeva śāstreṣu paribhāṣitam

plain_english: He is the single hero, then the paired one, having three powers and a fourfold nature, having five forms, this one with a sixfold nature, adorned as sevenfold and eightfold.
sanskrit_cite: ekavīro yāmalo@tha triśaktiścaturātmakaḥ pañcamūrtiḥ ṣaḍātmāyaṃ saptako@ṣṭakabhūṣitaḥ

plain_english: He has a ninefold nature, the power of the ten directions, and an elevenfold nature; thus Bhairava is the lord of the great twelve-spoked wheel.
sanskrit_cite: navātmā daśadikchaktirekādaśakalātmakaḥ dvādaśāramahācakranāyako bhairavastviti

plain_english: Thus, in the wheel of the universe—whether thousand-spoked or even uncountably spoked—the Lord, the great sovereign whose power is the universe, expands.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ yāvatsahasrāre niḥsaṃkhyāre@pi vā prabhuḥ viśvacakre maheśāno viśvaśaktirvijṛmbhate

plain_english: Even among those wheels, the differences belonging to each wheel are explained, case by case, through a unity that follows the nature of its own group.
sanskrit_cite: teṣāmapi ca cakrāṇā svavargānugamātmanā aikyena cakrago bhedastatra tatra nirūpitaḥ

plain_english: In the Traiśirasa doctrine, by the reckoning of four, six, two, and two, the Lord—whose own form is wondrous—is said to have sovereignty over six wheels.
sanskrit_cite: catuṣṣaḍdvirdvigaṇanāyogāttraiśirase mate ṣaṭcakreśvaratā nāthasyoktā citranijākṛteḥ

plain_english: There, the names of the goddesses of the wheel are determined according to differences of function and by etymological conception of the yoginīs associated with gentle or fierce forms and meditations.
sanskrit_cite: nāmāni cakradevīnāṃ tatra kṛtyavibhedataḥ saumyaraudrākṛtidhyānayogīnyanvarthakalpanāt

plain_english: For the one lord of consciousness, the inner body is indeed creative intuition; as gentle or in another measured form, the wheel of waves of consciousness is worshipped.
sanskrit_cite: ekasya saṃvinnāthasya hyāntarī pratibhā tanuḥ saumyaṃ vānyanmitaṃ saṃvidūrmicakramupāsyate

plain_english: With the intention, 'May this be nourished,' the goddess-consciousness is nourished by such meditation mixed with articulate expression, and also by external activity.
sanskrit_cite: asya syātpuṣṭirityeṣā saṃviddevī tathoditāt dhyānātsaṃjalpasaṃmiśrād vyāpārāccāpi bāhyataḥ

plain_english: When it becomes clear, it shines and grants him a corresponding fruit. Nourishment is like a dry place becoming a lake; therefore there is clear water.
sanskrit_cite: sphuṭībhūtā satī bhāti tasya tādṛkphalapradā puṣṭiḥ śuṣkasya sarasībhāvo jalamataḥ sitam

plain_english: Then, having followed that, meditation centered on it is extended; and there are phonemes which by their own nature flow with essence, as follows.
sanskrit_cite: anugamya tato dhyānaṃ tatpradhānaṃ pratanyate ye ca svabhāvato varṇā rasaniḥṣyandino yathā

plain_english: Those phonemes, mostly dental, labial, and dental, formed together with certain other sounds, attain the state of a seed and make that consciousness clear.
sanskrit_cite: dantyauṣṭhyadantyaprāyāste kaiścidvarṇaiḥ kṛtāḥ saha taṃ bījabhāvamāgatya saṃvidaṃ sphuṭayanti tām

plain_english: Even thought-natured speech would not fill that very nourishment.
sanskrit_cite: puṣṭiṃ kuru rasenainamāpyāyaya tarāmiti saṃjalpo@pi vikalpātmā kiṃ tāmeva na pūrayet

plain_english: This is nectar, this is milk, ghee brings strength; by that nourish his seed and fill the action.
sanskrit_cite: amṛteyamidaṃ kṣīramidaṃ sarpirbalāvaham tenāsya bījaṃ puṣṇīyāmityenāṃ pūrayetkriyām

plain_english: Therefore world-lord knowledge-Bhairava is worshipped by people desiring enjoyment and liberation, through limited and unlimited means.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādviśveśvaro bodhabhairavaḥ samupāsyate avacchedānavacchidbhyāṃ bhogamokṣārthibhirjanaiḥ

plain_english: Therefore the teacher instructed: those who know something apart from knowledge as sacrificial are even devotees of other deities.
sanskrit_cite: ye@pyanyadevatābhaktā ityato gururādiśat ye bodhādvyatiriktaṃ hi kiṃcidyājyatayā viduḥ

plain_english: They too, distinguishing the knowable, think through non-difference from knowledge, by the nature of unbroken I-awareness manifestation.
sanskrit_cite: te@pi vedyaṃ viviñcānā bodhābhedena manvate tenāvicchinnatāmarśarūpāhantāprathātmanaḥ

plain_english: For the self-manifest there is no injunction prior; indeed deity-creation has arisen from power-cause.
sanskrit_cite: svayaṃ-prathasya na vidhiḥ sṛṣṭyātmāsya ca pūrvagaḥ vedyā hi devatāsṛṣṭiḥ śakterhetoḥ samutthitā

plain_english: But awareness is eternal and self-manifest in I-form; injunction is three-part command, and meditation is injunction-nature.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃrūpā tu saṃvittirnityā svaprathanātmikā vidhirniyogastryaṃśā ca bhāvanā codanātmikā

plain_english: Indra and other deities are accomplished through injunction, but I-knowledge is not so; they take knowable form.
sanskrit_cite: tadekasiddhā indrādyā vidhipūrvā hi devatāḥ ahaṃbodhastu na tathā te tu saṃvedyarūpatām

plain_english: Seeing him only submerged, even knowing, they do not know; as said, they do not know me truly, therefore they wander.
sanskrit_cite: unmagnāmeva paśyantastaṃ vidanto@pi no viduḥ taduktaṃ na vidurmāṃ tu tattvenātaścalanti te

plain_english: But wandering is only attainment of limited form, as in 'gods and sacrificers go,' and by that it was described.
sanskrit_cite: calanaṃ tu vyavacchinnarūpatāpattireva yā devāndevayajo yāntītyādi tena nyarūpyata

plain_english: Those who, immersing knowability, know the consciousness-filled state there—even those devotees go to me, the unlimited.
sanskrit_cite: nimajjya vedyatāṃ ye tu tatra saṃvinmayīṃ sthitim viduste hyanavacchinnaṃ tadbhaktā api yānti mām

plain_english: Everywhere here the word I denotes awareness only; it is indicated by enjoyer and lord words as sacrificial-sacrificer status.
sanskrit_cite: sarvatrātra hyahaṃśabdo bodhamātraikavācakaḥ sa bhoktṛprabhuśabdābhyāṃ yājyayaṣṭṭatayoditaḥ

plain_english: Sacrificer-ship is awareness only; the sacrificial is not other. No form is established as another deity.
sanskrit_cite: yājamānī saṃvideva yājyā nānyeti coditam na tvākṛtiḥ kuto@pyanyā devatā na hi socitā

plain_english: Injunction is not said here, nor mantra or operation-abode; this self, covering itself, is situated and has gone to inert state.
sanskrit_cite: vidhiśca noktaḥ ko@pyatra mantrādi vṛttidhāma vā so@yamātmānamāvṛtya sthito jaḍapadaṃ gataḥ

plain_english: But the covered-uncovered self reaches from gods to immobile; the duality of this inert and non-inert is a wonder.
sanskrit_cite: āvṛtānāvṛtātmā tu devādisthāvarāntagaḥ jaḍājaḍasyāpyetasya dvairūpyasyāsti citratā

plain_english: Its freedom-nature indeed thinks what is not thought; as said in Trishiras scripture, one who knows the awakened thus knows that knowable-nature is consciousness-nature, and that shadow does not cover it.
sanskrit_cite: tasya svatantrabhāvo hi kiṃ kiṃ yanna vicintayet taduktaṃ triśiraḥśāstre saṃbuddha iti vetti yaḥ jñeyabhāvo hi ciddharmastacchāyācchādayenna tām

plain_english: By that, variety is situated in many ways in the uncovered portion of the non-inert part, named atom and so on.
sanskrit_cite: tenājaḍasya bhāgasya pudgalāṇvādisaṃjñinaḥ anāvaraṇabhāgāṃśe vaicitryaṃ bahudhā sthitam

plain_english: In awareness-form there is no real difference, although fixed; yet it is perceived by degree of covering removal.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvidrūpe na bhedo@sti vāstavo yadyapi dhruve tathāpyāvṛtinirhāsatāratamyātsa lakṣyate

plain_english: We will say that in detail in the determination of grace-descent; completing, otherness and grossness will be discussed.
sanskrit_cite: tadvistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ śaktipātavinirṇaye samāpya paratāṃ sthaulyaprasaṃge carcayiṣyate

plain_english: Therefore the lord manifests toward some knower his own full form, by a sequence of partial aspects.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ kaṃcitpramātāraṃ prati prathayate vibhuḥ pūrṇameva nijaṃ rūpaṃ kaṃcidaṃśāṃśikākramāt

plain_english: Indeed, manifestation of world-nature as one self-form is supreme knowledge for atoms; other knowledge is inferior and much.
sanskrit_cite: viśvabhāvaikabhāvātmasvarūpaprathanaṃ hi yat aṇūnāṃ tatparaṃ jñānaṃ tadanyadaparaṃ bahu

plain_english: That, manifesting by direct means and by that means etc., differs here by various breaks.
sanskrit_cite: tacca sākṣādupāyena tadupāyādināpi ca prathamānaṃ vicitrābhirbhaṃgībhiriha bhidyate

plain_english: There also, because self-other door-gate-ness is partial, greater difference arises by obstruction and non-obstruction.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpi svaparadvāradvāritvātsarvaśoṃśaśaḥ vyavadhānāvyavadhinā bhūyānbhedaḥ pravartate

plain_english: The means of knowledge is not called ignorance; knowledge only is subtle, supreme, and of will-nature, according to opinion.
sanskrit_cite: jñānasya cābhyupāyo yo na tadajñānamucyate jñānameva tu tatsūkṣmaṃ paraṃ tvicchātmakaṃ matam

plain_english: In knowledge, the distinction between means and goal is a coarse level. This very same thing is the power of action, which alone causes both bondage and liberation.
sanskrit_cite: upāyopeyabhāvastu jñānasya sthaulyaviśramaḥ eṣaiva ca kriyāśaktirbandhamokṣaikakāraṇam

plain_english: In the first mode, which is self-awareness resting in a single non-conceptual abode, whatever flashes forth clearly and directly is called will.
sanskrit_cite: tatrādye svaparāmarśe nirvikalpaikadhāmani yatsphuretprakaṭaṃ sākṣāttadicchākhyaṃ prakīrtitam

plain_english: Just as an object can appear clearly to someone whose perception has flashed forth, even without any deliberate mental connection, so too for some people the state of being Śiva shines forth directly.
sanskrit_cite: yathā visphuritadṛśāmanusandhiṃ vināpyalam bhāti bhāvaḥ sphuṭastadvatkeṣāmapi śivātmatā

plain_english: But when recognition does not come immediately, they call it the means of knowledge: through repeatedly working with conceptual elements in a steady sequence of certainty, one comes to reflective awareness.
sanskrit_cite: bhūyo bhūyo vikalpāṃśaniścayakramacarcanāt yatparāmarśamabhyeti jñānopāyaṃ tu tadviduḥ

plain_english: But what is taught as the means of action works by accomplishing externalized objects shaped by conceptual thought. Because it remains within difference, it does not by itself lead to liberation.
sanskrit_cite: yattu tatkalpanāklṛptabahirbhūtārthasādhanam kriyopāyaṃ tadāmnātaṃ bhedo nātrāpavargagaḥ

plain_english: For in the teaching of the revered scripture, there is no action separate from knowledge. Knowledge itself, when firmly established in that way, reaches the culmination of yoga.
sanskrit_cite: yato nānyā kriyā nāma jñānameva hi tattathā rūḍheryogāntatāṃ prāptamiti śrīgamaśāsane

plain_english: Yoga is not different from action, and action is not different from yoga. The cognition that is firmly grounded in reality and brings the impressions of one's own mind to rest is what is called action.
sanskrit_cite: yogo nānyaḥ kriyā nānyā tattvārūḍhā hi yā matiḥ svacittavāsanāśāntau sā kriyetyabhidhīyate

plain_english: In one's own mind there are latent impressions born from karma, impurity, and maya. The cognition that arises to calm those impressions is essentially of the nature of consciousness itself.
sanskrit_cite: svacitte vāsanāḥ karmamalamāyāprasūtayaḥ tāsāṃ śāntinimittaṃ yā matiḥ saṃvitsvabhāvikā

plain_english: That same cognition, which rests upon the outer range of principles that give rise to the body, is action. And that very same cognition becomes yoga when it dissolves those principles back into consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: sā dehārambhibāhyasthatattvabrātādhiśāyinī kriyā saiva ca yogaḥ syāttattvānāṃ cillayīkṛtau

plain_english: Even in everyday life, when one thinks 'I am going', there is first just an inner flash. That same flash enters the body, the place, and the senses, and then it becomes the act of going.
sanskrit_cite: loke@pi kila gacchāmītyevamantaḥ sphuraiva yā sā dehaṃ deśamakṣāṃścāpyāviśantī gatikriyā

plain_english: Therefore, even what is called action is really nothing but knowledge. For that reason, it is right to say that knowledge alone brings liberation, and this has already been stated.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātkriyāpi yā nāma jñānameva hi sā tataḥ jñānameva vimokṣāya yuktaṃ caitadudāhṛtam

plain_english: Liberation is nothing other than the unfolding of one's own true nature. And the self's true nature is nothing other than consciousness. The verse then turns to what comes next.
sanskrit_cite: mokṣo hi nāma naivānyaḥ svarūpaprathanaṃ hi saḥ svarūpaṃ cātmanaḥ saṃvinnānyattatra tu yāḥ punaḥ

plain_english: The powers of action and the rest are grounded in the nature of consciousness, because they cannot belong to anything unconscious, and no separate substrate for them can be established.
sanskrit_cite: kriyādikāḥ śaktayastāḥ saṃvidrūpādhikā nahi asaṃvidrūpatāyogāddharmiṇaścānirūpaṇāt

plain_english: In the scripture of the Supreme Lord, the powers are not said to have any separate substrate, as if they were qualities in the manner taught by the followers of Kaṇāda.
sanskrit_cite: parameśvaraśāstre hi na ca kāṇādadṛṣṭivat śaktīnāṃ dharmarūpāṇāmāśrayaḥ ko@pi kathyate

plain_english: If the powers of seeing, action, will, and so on were truly separate, then saying 'Shiva is one' would become mere words without any real basis.
sanskrit_cite: tataśca dṛkkriyecchādyā bhinnāścecchaktayastathā ekaḥ śiva itīyaṃ vāgvastuśūnyaiva jāyate

plain_english: For this reason, freedom is nothing but consciousness itself; and when examined closely, it is seen to unfold into many powers.
sanskrit_cite: tasmātsaṃvittvamevaitatsvātantryaṃ yattadapyalam vivicyamānaṃ bahvīṣu paryavasyati śaktiṣu

plain_english: Since liberation is the self's own shining forth, there is no reason to think that merely knowing a cause and its effect will automatically bring liberation.
sanskrit_cite: yataścātmaprathā mokṣastannehāśaṅkyamīdṛśam nāvaśyaṃ kāraṇātkārya tajjñānyapi na mucyate

plain_english: Although knowledge is sometimes described as the cause of liberation, that is not the primary way to understand their relation; so the objection raised earlier does not hold.
sanskrit_cite: yato jñānena mokṣasya yā hetuphalatoditā na sā mukhyā tato nāyaṃ prasaṃga iti niścitam

plain_english: Action is by nature knowledge itself, but as it takes on a grosser form in the self, its variety becomes visible.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ jñānasvabhāvaiva kriyā sthūlatvamātmani yato vahati tenāsyāṃ citratā dṛśyatāṃ kila

plain_english: Within the path of action, the means are divided into inner and outer and then into many further kinds, so they become countless.
sanskrit_cite: kriyopāye@bhyupāyānāṃ grāhyabāhyavibhedinām bhedopabhedavaividhyānniḥsaṃkhyatvamavāntarāt

plain_english: This also removes the doubt some wise people had, that because the means differ, liberation itself might differ.
sanskrit_cite: anena caitatpradhvastaṃ yatkecana śaśaṅkire upāyabhedānmokṣe@pi bhedaḥ syāditi sūrayaḥ

plain_english: Even if liberation comes about through different causes, such as the destruction of impurity and its power or the falling away of concealment, liberation itself is not different, just as the breaking of a pot is one kind of event though caused in different ways.
sanskrit_cite: malatacchaktividhvaṃsatirobhūcyutimadhyataḥ hetubhede@pi no bhinnā ghaṭadhvaṃsādivṛttivat

plain_english: This threefold division was taught by the Supreme Lord in the scripture called Śrīpūrva, in the section that determines the nature of penetration.
sanskrit_cite: tadetattrividhatvaṃ hi śāstre śrīpūrvanāmani ādeśi parameśitrā samāveśavinirṇaye

plain_english: When a person who is thinking of nothing at all is awakened by the teacher and penetration arises, that is called the śāmbhava penetration.
sanskrit_cite: akiṃciccintakasyaiva guruṇā pratibodhataḥ utpadyate ya āveśaḥ śāmbhavo@sāvidīritaḥ

plain_english: When one contemplates a reality without utterance, using the mind alone, and attains penetration in that way, it is called the śākta penetration.
sanskrit_cite: uccārarahitaṃ vastu cetasaiva vicintayan yaṃ samāveśamāpnoti śāktaḥ so@trābhidhīyate

plain_english: The penetration that arises through utterance, bodily practice, meditation, letters, and imagined locations is properly called the āṇava penetration.
sanskrit_cite: uccārakaraṇadhyānavarṇasthānaprakalpanaiḥ yo bhavetsa samāveśaḥ samyagāṇava ucyate

plain_english: The expression 'one who thinks of nothing' means that conceptual construction is not in use, and through that there is a sudden absorption into what is to be known.
sanskrit_cite: akiṃciccintakasyeti vikalpānupayogitā tayā ca jhaṭiti jñeyasamāpattirnirūpyate

plain_english: How does that happen? It happens through a most weighty teacher, whose awareness is turned toward the knowable and whose awakening is immediately mature.
sanskrit_cite: sā kathaṃ bhavatītyāha guruṇātigarīyasā jñeyābhimukhabodhena drākprarūḍhatvaśālinā

plain_english: The verse gives a grammatical explanation of the earlier expression and adds that, for the dependent self, penetration means sinking into its own true form.
sanskrit_cite: tṛtīyārthe tasi vyākhyā vā vaiyadhikaraṇyataḥ āveśaścāsvatantrasya svatadrūpanimajjanāt

plain_english: The meaning here is that one comes to share the nature of Shambhu, the primal Lord who is never separate from his power; this meaning is to be understood as shining forth on its own.
sanskrit_cite: paratadrūpatā śambhorādyācchaktyavibhāginaḥ tenāyamatra vākyārtho vijñeyaṃ pronmiṣatsvayam

plain_english: Even without any determinate judgment, it suddenly appears reflected in the mirror of the subject, overwhelms the subject, and displays its own majesty.
sanskrit_cite: vināpi niścayena drāk mātṛdarpaṇabimbitam mātāramadharīkurvat svāṃ vibhūtiṃ pradarśayat

plain_english: Depending on the degree of purity of the heart, the knowable appears in two ways: as mere consciousness, or as something inert and constructed.
sanskrit_cite: āste hṛdayanairmalyātiśaye tāratamyataḥ jñeyaṃ dvidhā ca cinmātraṃ jaḍaṃ cādyaṃ ca kalpitam

plain_english: The other kind of knowable is also treated as real in its own way; penetration into what is inert takes the form of a reflected image.
sanskrit_cite: itarattu tathā satyaṃ tadvibhāgo@yamīdṛśaḥ jaḍena yaḥ samāveśaḥ sapraticchandakākṛtiḥ

plain_english: Penetration into consciousness is nothing other than identity with it; for that reason the awareness involved is non-conceptual and does not depend on contemplation or similar practices.
sanskrit_cite: caitanyena samāveśastādātmyaṃ nāparaṃ kila tenāvikalpā saṃvittirbhāvanādyanapekṣiṇī

plain_english: Here śāmbhava penetration is the attainment of identity with Shiva; any determinate understandings that arise afterward come by its grace, not as its cause.
sanskrit_cite: śivatādātmyamāpannā samāveśo@tra śāṃbhavaḥ tatprasādātpunaḥ paścādbhāvino@tra viniścayāḥ

plain_english: Even if later determinate understandings arise in harmony with that identity, they cannot be its means, because they depend on conceptual construction, while the valid cognition in question is non-conceptual.
sanskrit_cite: santu tādātmyamāpannā na tu teṣāmupāyatā vikalpāpekṣayā mānamavikalpamiti bruvan

plain_english: This has already been answered, for what has been grasped is then followed by conceptual thought. Determinate cognition shines forth very clearly, so the objection does not stand.
sanskrit_cite: pratyukta eva siddhaṃ hi vikalpenānugamyate gṛhītamiti suspaṣṭā niścayasya yataḥ prathā

plain_english: By the force of unity with the nonconceptual sense of I grasp, the object is apprehended. In nonconceptual self-awareness, it is simply the flashing forth of the object that is known.
sanskrit_cite: gṛhṇāmītyavikalpaikyabalāttu pratipadyate avikalpātmasaṃvittau yā sphurattaiva vastunaḥ

plain_english: That flashing forth is not established by conceptual thought, since conceptual thought does not directly depend on the object. It belongs only to awareness, which rests in its own clarity or lack of clarity.
sanskrit_cite: sā siddhirna vikalpāttu vastvapekṣāvivarjitāt kevalaṃ saṃvidaḥ so@yaṃ nairmalyetaraviśramaḥ

plain_english: Both independence from and dependence on conceptual thought can occur in the same self. For example, even at night a jewel expert may see gems revealed only for the brief moment of a lightning flash.
sanskrit_cite: yadvikalpānapekṣatvasāpekṣatve nijātmani niśīthe@pi maṇijñānī vidyutkālapradarśitān

plain_english: He can discern the particular features of many jewels. If awareness is clear, this happens through the force of prior practice.
sanskrit_cite: tāṃstānviśeṣāṃścinute ratnānāṃ bhūyasāmapi nairmalyaṃ saṃvidaścedaṃ pūrvābhyāsavaśādatho

plain_english: This will be discussed later as arising from the will of the unrestricted Lord. The immersion has been described as having fifty forms.
sanskrit_cite: aniyantreśvarecchāta ityetaccarcayiṣyate pañcāśadvidhatā cāsya samāveśasya varṇitā

plain_english: This division is based on the clear distinctions within the thirty-six principles. Among them is a triad made of self, knowledge, and power.
sanskrit_cite: tattvaṣaṭtriṃśakaitatsthasphuṭabhedābhisandhitaḥ etattattvāntare yatpuṃvidyāśaktyātmakaṃ trayam

plain_english: In order, the triad called self, knowledge, and power is divided into four, ten, and three forms. This is because that triad is all-pervading.
sanskrit_cite: ambhodhikāṣṭhājvalanasaṃkhyairbhedairyataḥ kramāt puṃvidyāśaktisaṃjñaṃ yattatsarvavyāpakaṃ yataḥ

plain_english: So this triad is counted in distinction from the nonpervading principles. It also stands in mutual relation through impurity, the process of purification, and purity.
sanskrit_cite: avyāpakebhyastenedaṃ bhedena gaṇitaṃ kila aśuddhiśuddhyamānatvaśuddhitastu mitho@pi tat

plain_english: The elements are established by direct perception and can also be inferred from cause and effect. For that reason they are treated as separate from the group of principles.
sanskrit_cite: bhūtānyadhyakṣasiddhāni kāryahetvanumeyataḥ tattvavargātpṛthagbhūtasamākhyānyata eva hi

plain_english: The elements are within the range of all cognition, so the knowers place them in the fourfold scheme. There they find the proper room for their abiding.
sanskrit_cite: sarvapratītisadbhāvagocaraṃ bhūtameva hi viduścatuṣṭaye cātra sāvakāśe tadāsthitim

plain_english: The immersion of Rudra's power is said to be fivefold. But then what room would there be for it in the description of elemental immersion and the other forms?
sanskrit_cite: rudraśaktisamāveśaḥ pañcadhā nanu carcyate ko@vakāśo bhavettatra bhautāveśādivarṇane

plain_english: If one objects that such absorption can arise by contextual association, that is possible; but it is not for us, because people have different tastes and this absorption excludes the ordinary mind.
sanskrit_cite: prasaṃgādetaditicetsamādhiḥ saṃbhavannayam nāsmākaṃ mānasāvarjī loko bhinnaruciryataḥ

plain_english: It is said that in dualistic teachings the elements and so on are regarded as separated from the supreme Lord, but in this teaching, which is free from duality, it is not so.
sanskrit_cite: ucyate dvaitaśāstreṣu parameśādvibheditā bhūtādīnāṃ yathā sātra na tathā dvayavarjite

plain_english: All that is the thirty-sixfold reality, and whatever else there may be, all of that is the great Goddess, the unobstructed power of Rudra.
sanskrit_cite: yāvānṣaṭtriṃśakaḥ so@yaṃ yadanyadapi kiṃcana etāvatī mahādevī rudraśaktiranargalā

plain_english: For that very reason, in the second section the universal nature of earth and the other realities was expounded through divisions such as the fifteenfold scheme.
sanskrit_cite: tata eva dvitīye@sminnadhikāre nyarūpyata dharāderviśvarūpatvaṃ pāñcadaśyādibhedataḥ

plain_english: Therefore, just as in the earlier discussion awareness of the partless reality was understood through aspects such as qualities, parts, and wholes, so too it should be understood here.
sanskrit_cite: tasmādyathā purasthe@rthe guṇādyaṃśāṃśikāmukhāt niraṃśabhāvasaṃbodhastathaivātrāpi budhyatām

plain_english: Therefore, through properties such as nonconceptuality, firmness, and majesty, or through other properties that are inherent power-forms, the reality can be approached.
sanskrit_cite: ata evāvikalpatvadhrauvyaprābhavavaibhavaiḥ anyairvā śaktirūpatvāddharmaiḥ svasamavāyibhiḥ

plain_english: Thus, those whose mental impressions arise from streams of concepts awakened by scripture worship that all-pervading supreme Lord, either wholly or in part.
sanskrit_cite: sarvaśo@pyatha vāṃśena taṃ vibhuṃ parameśvaram upāsate vikalpaughasaṃskārādye śrutotthitāt

plain_english: Through their skill in the properties that shine within their own concepts, they come to rest upon the bearer of those properties as non-different and filled with the fullness of all properties.
sanskrit_cite: te tattatsvavikalpāntaḥsphurattaddharmapāṭavāt dharmiṇaṃ pūrṇadharmaughamabhedenādhiśerate

plain_english: For this reason the lord of Śrīvidyā respectfully said: if conceptual construction did not make your nonconceptual nature an object for sense-born cognition, then clear experiences with varied images inscribed within would not arise.
sanskrit_cite: ūcivānata eva śrīvidyādhipatirādarāt tvatsvarūpamavikalpamakṣajā kalpane na viṣayīkaroti cet antarullikhitacitrasaṃvido no bhaveyuranubhūtayaḥ sphuṭāḥ

plain_english: This is stated in the Śrīmataṅga and other texts, where the abode of the Lord is described, with various qualifications, as consisting of the rays of his own power.
sanskrit_cite: taduktaṃ śrīmataṅgādau svaśaktikiraṇātmakam atha patyuradhiṣṭhānamityādyuktaṃ viśeṣaṇaiḥ

plain_english: In that divine light there is a brilliantly radiant, motionless presence with an unmoving form; that alone is the supreme, subtle culmination, whose nature is nectar in all directions.
sanskrit_cite: tasyāṃ divi sudīptātmā niṣkampo@calamūrtimān kāṣṭhā saiva parā sūkṣmā sarvadikkāmṛtātmikā

plain_english: With all coverings destroyed, peaceful, intent on reality alone, free from beginning and end, and pure, that state is nevertheless spoken of figuratively as having a form.
sanskrit_cite: pradhvastāvaraṇā śāntā vastumātrātilālasā ādyantoparatā sādhvī mūrtitvenopacaryate

plain_english: This figurative way of speaking has a clear reason and purpose: through it clarity quickly arises in the qualified subject, and that leads to abiding in full absorption in that reality.
sanskrit_cite: tathopacārasyātraitannimitaṃ saprayojanam tanmukhā sphuṭatā dharmiṇyāśu tanmayatāsthitiḥ

plain_english: Those very qualities, called powers, are worshipped in various fitting forms so that one may become fully absorbed in that reality.
sanskrit_cite: ta eva dharmāḥ śaktyākhyāstaistairucitarūpakaiḥ ākāraiḥ paryupāsyante tanmayībhāvasiddhaye

plain_english: In that context, an unlimited power or even limited powers may be drawn in, according to the principle by which what is invoked becomes present, and according to nearness or distance.
sanskrit_cite: tatra kācitpunaḥ śaktiranantā vā mitāśca vā ākṣipeddhavatāsattvanyāyāddūrāntikatvataḥ

plain_english: Because of its pervasiveness, that reality draws in all powers, along with fullness, luminosity, the nature of consciousness, and the state of being Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite: tena pūrṇasvabhāvatvaṃ prakāśatvaṃ cidātmatā bhairavatvaṃ viśvaśaktīrākṣipedvyāpakatvataḥ

plain_english: Sadashiva and the other principles below the highest, lacking full upward pervasion, can draw in powers only to the extent that their worship is near or far.
sanskrit_cite: sadāśivādayastūrdhvavyāptyabhāvādadhojuṣaḥ śaktīḥ samākṣipeyustadupāsāntikadūrataḥ

plain_english: In this condition, the path taught here is called the Shakta path: it is a conceptual course, because it works through distinctions and their counterparts.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ-bhāve ca śāktākhyo vaikalpikapathakramaḥ iha tūkto yatastasmāt pratiyogyavikalpakam

plain_english: One who is established in the nonconceptual path, by whatever route they enter—from the earth principle up to Sadashiva—through that very route becomes Shiva.
sanskrit_cite: avikalpapathārūḍho yena yena pathā viśet dharāsadāśivāntena tena tena śivībhavet

plain_english: In a pure heart, illumined by the first flash of that level, awareness comes to recognize itself as supreme Shiva through that very opening.
sanskrit_cite: nirmale hṛdaye prāgryasphuradbhūmyaṃśabhāsini prakāśe tanmukhenaiva saṃvitparaśivātmatā

plain_english: Thus, those who live close to the wise teacher know this good means, which partakes of supreme will-power, as the Shambhava immersion.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ parecchāśaktyaṃśasadupāyamimaṃ viduḥ śāmbhavākhyaṃ samāveśaṃ sumatyantenivāsinaḥ

plain_english: Now the Shakta mode is described: it works clearly through mind, intellect, thought, and ego-making, in a conceptual way, dealing with things like will that are, in reality, made of maya.
sanskrit_cite: śākto@tha bhaṇyate cetodhī-manohaṃkṛti sphuṭam savikalpatayā māyāmayamicchādi vastutaḥ

plain_english: The Shakta mode works through identification and through the sequence of intention and determination; even though it is a means based in maya, at its end it becomes nonconceptual.
sanskrit_cite: abhimānena saṃkalpādhyavasāyakrameṇa yaḥ śāktaḥ sa māyopāyo@pi tadante nirvikalpakaḥ

plain_english: The nonconceptual state that appears in a bound soul is indeed called Shambhava, but it is incomplete because of the defect of the limited knower; when that defect falls away, it blossoms fully.
sanskrit_cite: paśorvai yāvikalpā bhūrdaśā sā śāmbhavī param apūrṇā mātṛdaurātmyāttadapāye vikasvarā

plain_english: Thus, in the Shakta mode there is a conceptual level marked by the awareness of agency; even when that awareness is clear, it still involves contraction, as explained earlier.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ vaikalpikī bhūmiḥ śākte kartṛtvavedane yasyāṃ sphuṭe paraṃ tvasyāṃ saṃkocaḥ pūrvanītitaḥ

plain_english: Likewise, for one who is intent on dissolving the whole mass of contraction, that power becomes radiant and can bring about the inner appearance of whatever is desired.
sanskrit_cite: tathā saṃkocasaṃbhāravilāyanaparasya tu sā yatheṣṭāntarābhāsakāriṇī śaktirujjvalā

plain_english: One might ask whether conceptual cognition exists in the Anava means. The answer is that, as defined here, the Anava means is marked by the absence of utterance, so that kind of conceptual operation belongs to another means.
sanskrit_cite: nanu vaikalpikī kiṃ dhīrāṇave nāsti tatra sā anyopāyātra tūccārarahitatvaṃ nyarūpayat

plain_english: Here the word utterance covers outward expression and related operations. These are not what define the Shakta means, because the Shakta means is characterized by the play of difference and nondifference, which is the very nature of power.
sanskrit_cite: uccāraśabdenātroktā bahvantena tadādayaḥ śaktyupāye na santyete bhedābhedau hi śaktitā

plain_english: The limited self is defined by clear difference, and the Anava means based on that works through conceptual thought and determination; yet at its culmination it becomes nonconceptual.
sanskrit_cite: aṇurnāma sphuṭo bhedastadupāya ihāṇavaḥ vikalpaniścayātmaiva paryante nirvikalpakaḥ

plain_english: An objection arises: how could intellect, mind, ego, and the individual self pervade Shiva, since they exist below him? How, then, can such a teaching be stated?
sanskrit_cite: nanu dhī-mānasāhaṃkṛtpumāṃso vyāpnuyuḥ śivam nādhovartitayā tena kathitaṃ kathamīdṛśam

plain_english: The answer is that, in reality, it is Shiva alone. Being self-luminous, he conceals his own nature and then appears again in that very form.
sanskrit_cite: ucyate vastuto@smākaṃ śiva eva tathāvidhaḥ svarūpagopanaṃ kṛtvā svaprakāśaḥ punastathā

plain_english: Even in dualistic scriptures such as the Matanga, this is clearly explained: the light that appears in the lower levels is the established manifestation of Shiva himself, who pervades downward.
sanskrit_cite: dvaitaśāstre mataṅgādau cāpyetatsunirūpitam adhovyāptuḥ śivasyaiva sa prakāśo vyavasthitaḥ

plain_english: For this reason, the supreme state shines even on the level of intellect and mind.
sanskrit_cite: yena buddhi-manobhūmāvapi bhāti paraṃ padam

plain_english: Both of these immersions indeed move toward the ocean of the nonconceptual, but without firm establishment in that state, nothing at all is accomplished.
sanskrit_cite: dvāvapyetau samāveśau nirvikalpārṇavaṃ prati prayāta eva tadrūḍhiṃ vinā naiva hi kiṃcana

plain_english: One should not assume any difference in the fruit of awareness here; rather, it was indicated that conceptual construction has a primary role in this context.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvittiphalabhiccātra na prakalpyetyato@bravīt kalpanāyāśca mukhyatvamatraiva kila sūcitam

plain_english: Even in the view that makes validity depend on conceptual construction, the nonconceptual is still valid—but its validity is reached through the ordered sequence of those very concepts.
sanskrit_cite: vikalpāpekṣayā yo@pi prāmāṇyaṃ prāha tanmate tadvikalpakramopāttanirvikalpapramāṇatā

plain_english: One who does not know the truth of the jewel may first practice through the means of certainty; by attaining the meansless, non-conceptual state, that person is called a knower of the jewel.
sanskrit_cite: ratnatattvamavidvānprāṅniścayopāyacarcanāt anupāyāvikalpāptau ratnajña iti bhaṇyate

plain_english: Here the means of non-difference is called śāmbhava, the means of both difference and non-difference is called śākta, and the means of difference is called āṇava.
sanskrit_cite: abhedopāyamatroktaṃ śāmbhavaṃ śāktamucyate bhedābhedātmakopāyaṃ bhedopāyaṃ tadāṇavam

plain_english: In the end, within knowledge accompanied by means, the entire expanse of action will be included in a very clear form.
sanskrit_cite: ante jñāne@tra sopāye samastaḥ karmavistaraḥ prasphuṭenaiva rūpeṇa bhāvī so@ntarbhaviṣyati

plain_english: Action is not something other than knowledge; it is knowledge that has taken on a sequential form through the force of means, and this was stated earlier as action.
sanskrit_cite: kriyā hi nāma vijñānānnānyadvastu kramātmatām upāyavaśataḥ prāptaṃ tatkriyeti puroditam

plain_english: Right knowledge, abiding in both self and other, is the sole cause of liberation, because the divisions of self, other, and so on are nothing more than constructions.
sanskrit_cite: samyagjñānaṃ ca muktyekakāraṇaṃ svaparasthitam yato hi kalpanāmātraṃ svaparādivibhūtayaḥ

plain_english: Even when all things are equally constructed, a teacher whose nature is the flashing forth of unity is called one-natured, accomplished, and liberated.
sanskrit_cite: tulye kālpanikatve ca yadaikyasphuraṇātmakaḥ guruḥ sa tāvadekātmā siddho muktaśca bhaṇyate

plain_english: As far as that continuum extends, it is declared to be the teacher; and because it is made of right knowledge, one is liberated by one's own self through it.
sanskrit_cite: yāvānasya hi saṃtāno gurustāvatsa kīrtitaḥ samyagjñānamayaśceti svātmanā mucyate tataḥ

plain_english: For that very reason the knower carries his own continuum across; this is well established by reason and scripture, because to that extent the sage is one.
sanskrit_cite: tata eva svasaṃtānaṃ jñānī tārayatītyadaḥ yuktyāgamābhyāṃ saṃsiddhaṃ tāvāneko yato muniḥ

plain_english: Therefore some object here: if liberation comes from knowledge, how could initiation and other ritual actions bring about liberation?
sanskrit_cite: tenātra ye codayanti nanu jñānādvimuktatā dīkṣādikā kriyā ceyaṃ sā kathaṃ muktaye bhavet

plain_english: If action is of the nature of knowledge, the objectors ask whether knowledge liberates only where it is located and what happens in liberating another; but they are dismissed at the root, and the text turns to what others have established.
sanskrit_cite: jñānātmā seti cejjñānaṃ yatrasthaṃ taṃ vimocayet anyasya mocane vāpi bhavetkiṃ nāsamañjasam iti te mūlataḥ kṣiptā yattvatrānyaiḥ samarthitam

plain_english: Some say impurity is a substance, like a film over the eye, and initiation is the action that removes it, like applying collyrium.
sanskrit_cite: malo nāma kila dravyaṃ cakṣuḥsthapaṭalādivat tadvihantrī kriyā dīkṣā tvañjanādikakarmavat

plain_english: We will refute that view later, since it is condemned by reason and scripture, and we will also show the true status of impurity, māyā, and karma.
sanskrit_cite: tatpurastānniṣetsyāmo yuktyāgamavigarhitam malamāyākarmaṇāṃ ca darśayiṣyāmahe sthitim

plain_english: Thus, in the knowledge that operates through the means of the three powers, the last is the root, above it is the middle, and above that is the highest, first level.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ śaktitrayopāyaṃ yajjñānaṃ tatra paścimam mūlaṃ taduttaraṃ madhyamuttarottaramādimam

plain_english: Even beyond that is a supreme knowledge, free of means and the rest, resting in the power of bliss; here it is called the unsurpassed.
sanskrit_cite: tato@pi paramaṃ jñānamupāyādivivarjitam ānandaśaktiviśrāntamanuttaramihocyate

plain_english: That self-luminous knowledge, whose true presence is rare even for the lords of knowledge and others, is spoken of in the revered Siddha Tantra.
sanskrit_cite: tatsvaprakāśaṃ vijñānaṃ vidyāvidyeśvarādibhiḥ api durlabhasadbhāvaṃ śrīsiddhātantra ucyate

plain_english: This is also clearly indicated in the Mālinī, in the eighteenth chapter, by the statement that it is not attained without the grace of Śaṅkara.
sanskrit_cite: mālinyāṃ sūcitaṃ caitatpaṭale@ṣṭādaśe sphuṭam na caitadaprasannena śaṃkareṇeti vākyataḥ

plain_english: By this very teaching in the Mālinīvijayottara, the fourfold knowledge that brings the great rise of accomplishment and liberation is systematized by me in this teaching called the Tantrāloka.
sanskrit_cite: ityanenaiva pāṭhena mālinīvijayottare iti jñānacatuṣkaṃ yatsiddhimuktimahodayam tanmayā tantryate tantrālokanāmnyatra śāsane

plain_english: Here, whatever is reflected on, whether inwardly or outwardly, first shines forth with its form not yet unfolded.
sanskrit_cite: tatreha yadyadantarvā bahirvā parimṛśyate anudghāṭitarūpaṃ tatpūrvameva prakāśate

plain_english: That first manifestation appears with an unopened, indescribable form; doubt arises only when some form is determined, and not otherwise.
sanskrit_cite: tathānudghāṭitākārā nirvācyenātmanā prathā saṃśayaḥ kutracidrūpe niścite sati nānyathā

plain_english: In the question 'what is this?', one part of the primary appearance is already well determined, while doubt remains because properties such as 'it is' or 'it is not' are not yet unfolded.
sanskrit_cite: etatkimiti mukhye@sminnetadaṃśaḥ suniścitaḥ saṃśayo@stitvanāstyādidharmānudghāṭitātmakaḥ

plain_english: The word 'what' does not reveal any additional meaning; it simply denotes the thing itself while its form remains unopened.
sanskrit_cite: kimityetasya śabdasya nādhiko@rthaḥ prakāśate kiṃ tvanunmudritākāraṃ vastvevābhidadhātyayam

plain_english: The doubt 'is it a post or a person?' is not the primary kind of doubt; it is really the arising of determination among many possible properties.
sanskrit_cite: sthāṇurvā puruṣo veti na mukhyo@styeṣa saṃśayaḥ bhūyaḥsthadharmajāteṣu niścayotpāda eva hi

plain_english: Again, doubt arises in the 'what' aspect because two forms that could be reflected on remain unopened; conceptual construction, by contrast, is clearly different.
sanskrit_cite: āmarśanīyadvairūpyānudghāṭanavaśātpunaḥ saṃśayaḥ sa kimityaṃśe vikalpastvanyathā sphuṭaḥ

plain_english: Therefore, the first manifestation of a being whose nature is not yet unfolded is here called indication, question, and indeed doubt.
sanskrit_cite: tenānudghāṭitātmatvabhāvaprathanameva yat prathamaṃ sa ihoddeśaḥ praśnaḥ saṃśaya eva ca

plain_english: As self-awareness expands along the path by which forms and beings that were not yet fully revealed come forth, it becomes the questioner and takes on the condition of the disciple.
sanskrit_cite: tathānudghāṭitākārabhāvaprasaravartmanā prasarantī svasaṃvittiḥ praṣṭrī śiṣyātmatāṃ gatā

plain_english: Because the certainty of inner reflective awareness is then concealed, the questioner also partakes in the rise of withdrawal that comes immediately after expansion.
sanskrit_cite: tathāntaraparāmarśaniścayātmatirohiteḥ prasarānantarodbhūtasaṃhārodayabhāgapi

plain_english: To whatever extent there is a clearly manifest outward expansion in which her own form has not yet fully opened, to that same extent she is called the questioner.
sanskrit_cite: yāvatyeva bhavedbāhyaprasare prasphuṭātmani anunmīlitarūpā sā praṣṭrī tāvati bhaṇyate

plain_english: In this way, awakening itself takes the form of question and answer; so even in the roles of teacher and disciple, the difference of bodies is not ultimately real.
sanskrit_cite: svayamevaṃ vibodhaśca tathā praśnottarātmakaḥ guruśiṣyapade@pyeṣa dehabhedo hyatāttvikaḥ

plain_english: Because awareness is of the nature of awareness, it makes the many forms that abide within it appear outwardly, just as both the general and specific features of a grape are manifested.
sanskrit_cite: bodho hi bodharūpatvādantarnānākṛtīḥ sthitāḥ bahirābhāsayatyeva drāksāmānyaviśeṣataḥ

plain_english: When some property is projected only in a general way, while a further specific aspect is still awaited, that general projection has the nature of doubt.
sanskrit_cite: srakṣyamāṇaviśeṣāṃśākāṃkṣāyogyasya kasyacit dharmasya sṛṣṭiḥ sāmānyasṛṣṭiḥ sā saṃśayātmikā

plain_english: When the awaited specific aspect finally settles, determination arises; it comes from the inclination of the cognizing subject, and not in any other way, not even through countless imagined alternatives.
sanskrit_cite: srakṣyamāṇo viśeṣāṃśo yadā tūparamettadā nirṇayo mātṛrucito nānyathā kalpakoṭibhiḥ

plain_english: Then, because of the skillful force with which that object is appropriated in its own nature, it opens up; and by that act arise determinations that follow upon its definition.
sanskrit_cite: tasyātha vastunaḥ svātmavīryākramaṇapāṭavāt unmudraṇaṃ tayākṛtyā lakṣaṇottaranirṇayāḥ

plain_english: Because each newly determined aspect of a property becomes the basis for what follows, examination proceeds again and again in the form of indication and definition.
sanskrit_cite: nirṇītatāvaddharmāṃśapṛṣṭhapātitayā punaḥ bhūyo bhūyaḥ samuddeśalakṣaṇātmaparīkṣaṇam

plain_english: In perception, inference, comparison, trustworthy testimony, and the rest, the triad of indication, definition, and examination shines forth in the cognition of all living beings.
sanskrit_cite: dṛṣṭānumānaupamyāptavacanādiṣu sarvataḥ uddeśalakṣaṇāvekṣātritayaṃ prāṇināṃ sphuret

plain_english: Indication is non-conceptual, definition is conceptual construction, and examination is a further series of conceptual constructions, even within direct perception.
sanskrit_cite: nirvikalpitamuddeśo vikalpo lakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ parīkṣaṇaṃ tathādhyakṣe vikalpānāṃ paramparā

plain_english: Saying 'this is a mountain' is indication; saying 'it has fire because there is smoke' is definition; and the whole network of knowledge about pervasion and the like is examination.
sanskrit_cite: nago@yamiti coddeśo dhūmitvādagnimāniti lakṣyaṃ vyāptyādivijñānajālaṃ tvatra parīkṣaṇam

plain_english: This enunciation is like a cow; the remainder becomes a definition in examination.
sanskrit_cite: uddeśo@yamiti prācyo gotulyo gavayābhidhaḥ iti vā lakṣaṇaṃ śeṣaḥ parīkṣopamitau bhavet

plain_english: Such an enunciation, with its own desire, defines the sacrifice command; agnishtoma and the remainder are examined.
sanskrit_cite: svaḥkāma īdṛguddeśo yajetetyasya lakṣaṇam agniṣṭomādinetyeṣā parīkṣā śeṣavartinī

plain_english: The creation of a thing, tolerating unwanted parts, is called enunciation.
sanskrit_cite: vikalpasrakṣyamāṇānyarucitāṃśasahiṣṇunaḥ vastuno yā tathātvena sṛṣṭiḥ soddeśasaṃjñitā

plain_english: Then only does one discern; future creation, arranged timelessly, connects all time.
sanskrit_cite: tadaiva saṃviccinute yāvataḥ srakṣyamāṇatā yato hyakālakalitā saṃdhatte sārvakālikam

plain_english: The creation of what will be created and withdrawal of the previously created part, when duty is declared, is called the mark of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: srakṣyamāṇasya yā sṛṣṭiḥ prāksṛṣṭāṃśasya saṃhṛtiḥ anūdyamāne dharme sā saṃvillakṣaṇamucyate

plain_english: The examination resting from creation and withdrawal is said, with a mother-approved fixed limit.
sanskrit_cite: tatpṛṣṭhapātibhūyoṃśasṛṣṭisaṃhāraviśramāḥ parīkṣā kathyate mātṛrucitā kalpitāvadhiḥ

plain_english: First seeing, then middle, then vaikhari: these are para, para-apara, and apara-natured goddesses.
sanskrit_cite: prākpaśyantyatha madhyānyā vaikharī ceti tā imāḥ parā parāparā devī caramā tvaparātmikā

plain_english: Desire and the three powers are declared; this practice is breathed and extended.
sanskrit_cite: icchādi śaktitritayamidameva nigadyate etatprāṇita evāyaṃ vyavahāraḥ pratāyate

plain_english: In the supreme teaching, question-answer nature has fivefold relation-nature.
sanskrit_cite: etatpraśnottarātmatve pārameśvaraśāsane parasaṃbandharūpatvamabhisaṃbandhapañcake

plain_english: As said in Ratnamala, all is other-art-natured: great interval, divine, mixed, and fifth.
sanskrit_cite: yathoktaṃ ratnamālāyāṃ sarvaḥ parakalātmakaḥ mahānavāntaro divyo miśro@nyo@nyastu pañcamaḥ

plain_english: The unity of distinct questioner and speaker is called relation, supremacy, full-unity manifesting.
sanskrit_cite: bhinnayoḥ praṣṭṛtadvaktroścaikātmyaṃ yatsa ucyate saṃbandhaḥ paratā cāsya pūrṇaikātmyaprathāmayī

plain_english: By this very method another relation is sufficient, scripture-declared through fullness union.
sanskrit_cite: anenaiva nayena syātsaṃbandhāntaramapyalam śāstravācyaṃ phalādīnāṃ paripūrṇatvayogataḥ

plain_english: Thus this consciousness-goddess is by nature always the breath of three enunciations and form of all scriptures.
sanskrit_cite: itthaṃ saṃvidiyaṃ devī svabhāvādeva sarvadā uddeśāditrayaprāṇā sarvaśāstrasvarūpiṇī

plain_english: There first enunciation has elder-younger distinction; knowledge-means and supreme third means are named.
sanskrit_cite: tatrocyate puroddeśaḥ pūrvajānujabhedavān vijñānabhidgatopāyaḥ paropāyastṛtīyakaḥ

plain_english: Shakti-means, human-means, time-means, seventh, wheel-rise, space-path, principle-path, principle-distinction.
sanskrit_cite: śāktopāyo naropāyaḥ kālopāyo@tha saptamaḥ cakrodayo@tha deśādhvā tattvādhvā tattvabhedanam

plain_english: Kalā-path use, power-descent concealment, initiation beginning, conventional initiation, hereditary rite.
sanskrit_cite: kalādyadhvādhvopayogaḥ śaktipātatirohitī dīkṣopakramaṇaṃ dīkṣā sāmayī pautrike vidhau

plain_english: Object-procedure, subtle initiation, immediate transcendence, balance initiation, indirect, linga-removal consecration.
sanskrit_cite: prameyaprakriyā sūkṣmā dīkṣā sadyaḥsamutkramaḥ tulādīkṣātha pārokṣī liṅgoddhāro@bhiṣecanam

plain_english: Final rite, shraddha arrangement, remainder conduct determination, linga worship, festival purification, occasion-caused.
sanskrit_cite: antyeṣṭiḥ śrāddhaklṛptiśca śeṣavṛttinirūpaṇam liṅgārcā bahubhitparvapavitrādi nimittajam

plain_english: Secret practice, mantra flood, mandala, seal rite, unification, entry into own nature, scripture union.
sanskrit_cite: rahasyacaryā mantraugho maṇḍalaṃ mudrikāvidhiḥ ekīkāraḥ svasvarūpe praveśaḥ śāstramelanam

plain_english: Future narration and scripture-authority determination; with seven added to thirty, the wise always...
sanskrit_cite: āyātikathanaṃ śāstropādeyatvanirūpaṇam iti saptādhikāmenāṃ triṃśataṃ yaḥ sadā budhaḥ

plain_english: Practicing daily rites, he becomes directly Bhairava; in thirty-seven, complete knowledge, he becomes Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite: āhnikānāṃ samabhyasyet sa sākṣādbhairavo bhavet saptatriṃśatsu saṃpūrṇabodho yadbhairavo bhavet

plain_english: What wonder, even small ones attain Bhairava-state by sight; this previous enunciation is said, now follower.
sanskrit_cite: kiṃ citramaṇavo@pyasya dṛśā bhairavatāmiyuḥ ityeṣa pūrvajoddeśaḥ kathyate tvanujo@dhunā

plain_english: In the knowledge section, enunciation of bharva in order; in the second section, means-distinction.
sanskrit_cite: vijñānabhitprakaraṇe bharvasyoddeśanaṃ kramāt dvitīyasminprakaraṇe gatopāyatvabheditā

plain_english: Universal consciousness reflection, recollection rise order, mantra nondifference in supreme means is distinguished.
sanskrit_cite: viśvacitpratibinbatvaṃ parāmarśodayakramaḥ mantrādyabhinnarūpatvaṃ paropāye vivicyate

plain_english: The refinement of conceptual thought, the principle of reasoning, the true nature of the teacher, the non-applicability of the limbs of yoga, and disregard for merely imagined worship and the like are treated here.
sanskrit_cite: vikalpasaṃskriyā tarkatattvaṃ gurusatattvakam yogāṅgānupayogitvaṃ kalpitārcādyanādaraḥ

plain_english: In the śākta approach, the arising of the wheel of consciousness, the true power of mantra, the real nature of recitation and related practices, and the equal standing of prohibition and injunction are discussed.
sanskrit_cite: saṃviccakrodayo mantravīrya japyādi vāstavam niṣedhavidhitulyatvaṃ śāktopāye@tra carcyate

plain_english: Meditation of the intellect, the conscious nature of the utterance of the vital principle, and utterance as the path of entry into the supreme principle are set forth here.
sanskrit_cite: buddhidhyānaṃ prāṇatattvasamuccāraścidātmatā uccāraḥ paratattvāntaḥpraveśapathalakṣaṇam

plain_english: The instrument and the principle of the phonemes are explained, and in the individual approach there is also the conceptualization of the moving cycles of day and night, transitions, and the like.
sanskrit_cite: karaṇaṃ varṇatattvaṃ cetyāṇave tu nirūpyate cāramānamahorātrasaṃkrāntyādivikalpanam

plain_english: In the conceptualization of the path of time, there is the varied play of withdrawal and the arising of phonemes, as well as the arising of the wheel designated by the mantras and vidyās that divide that wheel.
sanskrit_cite: saṃhāracitratā varṇodayaḥ kālādhvakalpane cakrabhinmantravidyābhidetaccakrodaye bhavet

plain_english: The measure of the worlds and their summary correlation with the principles are treated in the account of the path of space, and a corresponding pair is treated in the determination of the path of principles.
sanskrit_cite: parimāṇaṃ purāṇāṃ ca saṃgrahastattvayojanam etaddeśādhvanirdeśe dvayaṃ tattvādhvanirṇaye

plain_english: The relation of cause and effect, the explanation of the sequence of principles, the nature of reality, the classification of principles, and the explanation of waking and the other states are all treated here.
sanskrit_cite: kāryakāraṇabhāvaśca tattvakramanirūpaṇam vastudharmastattvavidhirjāgradādinirūpaṇam

plain_english: In the division of the principles, the division of cognizing subjects is examined, along with the nature of kalā and the ways the principles are grouped as one, three, five, and so forth.
sanskrit_cite: pramātṛbheda ityetat tattvabhede vicāryate kalāsvarūpamekatripañcādyaistattvakalpanam

plain_english: The sequence of the divisions of the phonemes and the explanation of the all-supporting power are analyzed to this extent within the investigation of the paths beginning with kalā.
sanskrit_cite: varṇabhedakramaḥ sarvādhāraśaktinirūpaṇam kalādyadhvavicārāntaretāvatpravivicyate

plain_english: In the application of the paths, the contemplation of non-difference, along with trembling and laughter, is treated, as well as the multiplication of impurities, their true nature, and the manifold variety of power.
sanskrit_cite: abhedabhāvanākampahāsau tvadhvopayojane saṃkhyādhikyaṃ malādīnāṃ tattvaṃ śaktivicitratā

plain_english: In the examination of the descent of power, the establishment of independence and the manifold variety of concealment are the topics summarized for discussion.
sanskrit_cite: anapekṣitvasiddhiśca tirobhāvavicitratā śaktipātaparīkṣāyāmetāvānvācyasaṃgrahaḥ

plain_english: At the commencement of initiation, concealment is removed through knowledge, fullness is attained, and departure from the body is shown to be unnecessary.
sanskrit_cite: tirobhāvavyapagamo jñānena paripūrṇatā utkrāntyanupayogitvaṃ dīkṣopakramaṇe sthitam

plain_english: In the examination of the student's fitness and related matters, the conception of places divided by location, the division of general nyāsa, the offering vessel, and their purpose are covered.
sanskrit_cite: śiṣyaucityaparīkṣādau sthānabhitsthānakalpanam sāmānyanyāsabhedo@rghapātraṃ caitatprayojanam

plain_english: The fitness of materials, worship, outer-door worship, sequential entry, the nature of initiation, and the purification of body, breath, and so on are outlined.
sanskrit_cite: dravyayogyatvamarcā ca bahirdvārārcanaṃ kramāt praveśo diksvarūpaṃ ca dehaprāṇādiśodhanam

plain_english: The variety of special nyāsa, the special offering vessel, worship of the body, and nyāsa and worship on the paths of breath, intellect, and consciousness are described.
sanskrit_cite: viśeṣanyāsavaicitryaṃ saviśeṣārghabhājanam dehapūjā prāṇabuddhicitsvadhvanyāsapūjane

plain_english: The superiority over other scriptural groups, worship of the wheel on all sides, taking possession of the site, the five cow products, and worship of the earth and Gaṇeśa are included.
sanskrit_cite: anyaśāstragaṇotkarṣaḥ pūjā cakrasya sarvataḥ kṣetragrahaḥ pañcagavyaṃ pūjanaṃ bhūgaṇeśayoḥ

plain_english: Worship of the weapon mantra, the fire rite, consecration related to fire, oblations of satisfaction, preparation of the rice offering, and rites ending with the tooth-stick are treated.
sanskrit_cite: astrārcā vahnikāryaṃ cāpyadhivāsanamagnigam tarpaṇaṃ carusaṃsiddhirdantakāṣṭhāntasaṃskriyā

plain_english: The rite of Śiva's hand, preparation of the bed, rites relating to dreams, and the observances are summarized.
sanskrit_cite: śivahastavidhiścāpi śayyāklṛptivicāraṇam svapnasya sāmayaṃ karma samayāśceti saṃgrahaḥ

plain_english: In the fifteenth chapter, on the rite of becoming an initiate, contemplation of the self of the maṇḍala and the elaboration of the offered victim are covered.
sanskrit_cite: samayitvavidhāvasminsyātpañcadaśa āhnike maṇḍalātmānusandhānaṃ nivedyapaśuvistaraḥ

plain_english: Satisfaction of the fire, illumination of one's own nature, the rite of nyāsa on the paths present in the student's body, and the variety of what is purified, the purifier, and so on are treated.
sanskrit_cite: agnitṛptiḥ svasvabhāvadīpanaṃ śiṣyadehagaḥ adhvanyāsavidhiḥ śodhyaśodhakādivicitratā

plain_english: In the sixteenth chapter, the division of initiation, the supreme nyāsa, the purpose of the being of mantra, and the division of yojanikā and related matters are presented.
sanskrit_cite: dīkṣābhedaḥ paro nyāso mantrasattāprayojanam bhedo yojanikādeśca ṣoḍaśe syādihāhnike

plain_english: In the rite of the son's initiation, the preparation of the thread, purification of the principles, burning of the bonds, application, and the division of the paths are stated.
sanskrit_cite: sūtraklṛptistattvaśuddhiḥ pāśadāho@tha yojanam adhvabhedastathetyevaṃ kathitaṃ pautrike vidhau

plain_english: In the eighteenth chapter, called the abbreviated initiation, the absence of birth and the like and a very clear division of mantras are treated.
sanskrit_cite: jananādivihīnatvaṃ mantrabhedo@tha susphuṭaḥ iti saṃkṣiptadīkṣākhye syādaṣṭādaśa āhnike

plain_english: In the rite of immediate departure, inspection of kalā, nyāsa of the sword and the like, movement occurring in the body, and the rite of brahma-vidyā are taught.
sanskrit_cite: kalāvekṣā kṛpāṇyādinyāsaścāraḥ śarīragaḥ brahmavidyāvidhiścaivamuktaṃ sadyaḥsamutkrame

plain_english: In the twentieth chapter, the full subject to be explained will be consecration ending with the examination of qualification, and also the rite of the balance.
sanskrit_cite: adhikāraparīkṣāntaḥsaṃskāro@tha tulāvidhiḥ ityetadvācyasarvasvaṃ syādviṃśatitamāhnike

plain_english: In the twenty-first chapter, the procedures to be explained are the rite of the dead and the living, the net, lordship over positions, the group of consecratory rites, and the examination of strength and weakness.
sanskrit_cite: mṛtajīvadvidhirjālo padeśaḥ saṃskriyāgaṇaḥ balābalavicāraścetyekaviṃśāhnike vidhiḥ

plain_english: In the procedure for removing the mark, what must be clearly explained is hearing, permission, purification, the removal of sin, and the cutting off of doubt.
sanskrit_cite: śravaṇaṃ cābhyanujñānaṃ śodhanaṃ pātakacyutiḥ śaṅkāccheda iti spaṣṭaṃ vācyaṃ liṅgoddhṛtikrame

plain_english: The examination and appointment of the teacher, his vow, the removal of the disciple's understanding, its divisions, and the state of being a sādhaka in the rite of consecration—this much is to be covered.
sanskrit_cite: parīkṣācāryakaraṇaṃ tadvrataṃ haraṇaṃ mateḥ tadvibhāgaḥ sādhakatvamabhiṣekavidhau tviyat

plain_english: The qualified person, the consecration, and its purpose—this is what is to be explained and discussed in the twenty-fourth chapter, called the final worship.
sanskrit_cite: adhikāryatha saṃskārastatprayojanamityadaḥ caturviṃśe@ntyayāgākhye vaktavyaṃ paricarcyate

plain_english: In the twenty-fifth chapter, in the exposition of śrāddha, the purpose—granting enjoyment and liberation—and the procedure are made clear, and the topics are summarized.
sanskrit_cite: prayojanaṃ bhogamokṣadānenātra vidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ pañcaviṃśāhnike śrāddhaprakāśe vastusaṃgrahaḥ

plain_english: The purpose of the remaining conduct, daily worship, the supreme worship on the altar, the nature of the liṅga in its many forms, and the explanation of the rosary are to be set forth.
sanskrit_cite: prayojanaṃ śeṣavṛtternityārcā sthaṇḍile parā liṅgasvarūpaṃ bahudhā cākṣasūtranirūpaṇam

plain_english: The divisions of worship are to be explained in the revelation of liṅga worship, and then the division, purpose, and procedure of occasional rites.
sanskrit_cite: pūjābheda iti vācyaṃ liṅgārcāsaṃprakāśane naimittikavibhāgastatprayojanavidhistataḥ

plain_english: The divisions of festivals, their specifics, circle worship and its performance, and the purpose of worship on guru days and other special beginning and end days are to be explained.
sanskrit_cite: parvabhedāstadviśeṣaścakracarcā tadarcanam gurvādyantadinādyarcāprayojananirūpaṇam

plain_english: The examination of death, the procedure for gatherings of yoginīs and others, the method of exposition, the method of hearing, and the procedure for guru worship are to be described.
sanskrit_cite: mṛteḥ parīkṣā yogīśīmelakādividhistathā vyākhyāvidhiḥ śrutavidhirgurupūjāvidhistviyat

plain_english: In the twenty-eighth chapter, called the revelation of occasional rites, are established the division of the qualified practitioner and the sequence of the lineage of siddhas and their consorts.
sanskrit_cite: naimittikaprakāśākhye @pyaṣṭāviṃśāhnike sthitam adhikāryātmano bhedaḥ siddhapatnīkulakramaḥ

plain_english: In the twenty-ninth chapter are the procedures of worship and of the messenger, the sequence of the secret upaniṣad, initiation, consecration, and awakening.
sanskrit_cite: arcāvidhirdautavidhī rahasyopaniṣatkramaḥ dīkṣābhiṣekau bodhaścetyekonatriṃśa āhnike

plain_english: In the thirtieth chapter, the nature of mantra and its power are explained. In the thirty-first, the division of the trident and lotus and the explanation of the sky, the swastika, and so on are to be set forth in detail.
sanskrit_cite: mantrasvarūpaṃ tadvīryamiti triṃśe nirūpitam śūlābjabhedo vyomaśasvastikādinirūpaṇam

plain_english: These matters are to be explained in detail in the thirty-first chapter. In the thirty-second chapter are set forth the distinctions of quality and principality, their own nature, and the worship of their power.
sanskrit_cite: vistareṇābhidhātavyamityekatriṃśa āhnike guṇapradhānatābhedāḥ svarūpaṃ vīryacarcanam

plain_english: The division of kalā is declared in the full revelation of the seals, because from the thirty-two principles up to Īśa it becomes clearly manifest there.
sanskrit_cite: kalābheda iti proktaṃ mudrāṇāṃ saṃprakāśane dvātriṃśatattvādīśākhyātprabhṛti prasphuṭo yataḥ

plain_english: Since there is no separate division here, no additional topic is stated in this overview. Even so, that matter is treated because it is primary and must be known in the sequence of another section.
sanskrit_cite: na bhedo@sti tato noktamuddeśāntaramatra tat mukhyatvena ca vedyatvādadhikārāntarakramaḥ

plain_english: Thus the method of enunciation has been declared for the sake of easy comprehension. Now, in examining its characteristics, they will be explained in due order.
sanskrit_cite: ityuddeśavidhiḥ proktaḥ sukhasaṃgrahahetave athāsya lakṣaṇāvekṣe nirūpyete yathākramam

plain_english: The self abides as partless consciousness-light, and its own nature is the host of powers of consciousness. It appears bound by concealing its own greatness, and its liberation comes through revealing its luminous nature. This manifold meaning has been briefly revealed here.
sanskrit_cite: ātmā saṃvitprakāśasthitiranavayavā saṃvidityāttaśaktivrātaṃ tasya svarūpaṃ sa ca nija mahasaśchādanādbaddharūpaḥ ātmajyotiḥsvabhāvaprakaṭanavidhinā tasya mokṣaḥ sa cāyaṃ citrākārasya citraḥ prakaṭita iha yatsaṃgraheṇārtha eṣaḥ

plain_english: False knowledge produces defects of vision like a cataract, so that even what is pure seems to be a place of impurity. But when that cataract-like defect in vision is recognized and removed, how could any suspicion of impurity remain?
sanskrit_cite: mithyājñānaṃ timiramasamān dṛṣṭidoṣānprasūte tatsadbhāvādvimalamapi tadbhāti mālinyadhāma yattu prekṣyaṃ dṛśi parigataṃ taimirīṃ doṣamudrāṃ dūraṃ runddhetprabhavatu kathaṃ tatra mālinyaśaṅkā

plain_english: O host of beings, you forcibly seize people's hearts, make them dance with many gestures, conceal the heart of the self, and sport in that way. Whoever calls you insentient is himself insentient and poorly taught in thinking himself sensitive; I would even take his insentience as a kind of praise, since it suggests a likeness to you.
sanskrit_cite: bhāvavrāta? haṭhājjanasya hṛdayānyākramya yannartayan bhaṅgībhirvividhābhirātmahṛdayaṃ pracchādya saṃkrīḍase yastvāmāha jaḍaṃ jaḍaḥ sahṛdayaṃmanyatvaduḥśikṣito manye@muṣya jaḍātmatā stutipadaṃ tvatsāmyasaṃbhāvanāt

plain_english: Here, teachers whose impurities have fallen away, who know the higher and the lower, and who are grounded in the true being of Shiva are authorized to undertake investigation. Without that qualification, inquiry is fruitless and leads only to hatred, blame, loss, and begging.
